core_obligations: Reduce the assertion to the statement that the structure sheaf of the etale site is a flat module over the pullback of the structure sheaf of the Zariski site (proof lines 3227-3230).

Identify that pullback as the sheafification of the presheaf sending an etale morphism V to S to the sections of the Zariski structure sheaf over the image of V, using that etale morphisms are open (proof lines 3231-3236).
Check flatness in the affine case: for V etale over S with V and f(V) affine, pass to the associated etale ring map and use that etale ring maps are flat (proof lines 3237-3242).

Show that every object of the etale site admits an affine open cover whose members have affine open image in S, by choosing an affine open inside V with affine image, taking an affine open neighbourhood of the image, and pulling it back, which is a fibre product and hence affine (proof lines 3243-3250).
Apply the flatness criterion for a refined covering to conclude flatness on the whole etale site (proof lines 3251-3252).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to flatness of the etale structure sheaf over the pulled-back Zariski structure sheaf (proof lines 3227-3230).
Compute the pulled-back structure sheaf via openness of etale morphisms (proof lines 3231-3236).
Flatness in the affine case, through etale ring maps (proof lines 3237-3242).
Existence of the required affine open cover, with the fibre product argument in the footnote (proof lines 3243-3250).
Conclude by the flatness criterion for refinements (proof lines 3251-3252).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the morphism of ringed sites from the small etale site of S to the small Zariski site of S is flat (statement lines 3220-3224). Flateness here is a statement about the structure sheaf of the etale site viewed as a module over the pullback of the Zariski structure sheaf, so the proof must first identify that pullback: using that etale morphisms are open, it computes it as the sheafification of the presheaf sending an etale V over S to the sections of the Zariski structure sheaf over the image of V (proof lines 3227-3236). It then checks flatness on the members of a suitable covering of each etale V: if both V and its image are affine, the map corresponds to an etale ring map, and etale ring maps are flat, so the comparison map between the two structure sheaves is flat there (proof lines 3237-3242). The remaining point is that every etale V does admit an affine open cover by pieces whose images are affine open in S, which the author proves in a footnote by intersecting with a suitable affine and taking a fibre product; flatness then descends from the covering by the sheafification-and-refinement criterion (proof lines 3243-3252). The claim is H2: three separate verifications are needed, the computation of the pullback sheaf, the flatness of the affine case through the corresponding ring map, and the affineness of the covering used to globalise, and all three are carried out rather than cited.
